summary: 1st American Nuclear Co. (FANCO) is developing EAGL-1, a 240 MWe fast-spectrum small modular reactor cooled by lead-bismuth, and proposes its own HALEU fuel fabrication facility. Its Bridge Power offer starts a site on conventional boilers and steam turbines, meant to swap in EAGL-1 later. Headquarters are in Indianapolis, reactor development in Richland, Washington.
oneLiner: Developing EAGL-1, a 240 MWe lead-bismuth-cooled fast reactor, and its own HALEU fuel fabrication
thesis: FANCO pairs energy with manufacturing: a 240 MWe reactor designed for factory fabrication, a proposed fuel plant, and a plan announced with the State of Indiana (reported at more than $4 billion) for manufacturing facilities and an energy park.
stage: Five Form Ds report $13,687,050 sold: $1,250,000 of $2,500,000 in equity (filed 30 June 2025), $20,000 of $5,000,000 in SAFEs (29 August 2025), $10,000,000 from one investor (15 December 2025), $1,417,050 from four (22 December 2025), and $1,000,000 of $25,000,000 in equity and debt from one investor (18 September 2026). The filings name no investors. No round announcement was found. The company targets power from EAGL-1 by 2033.

team.name: Bill Stokes
team.background: President and founder. The company site says he has more than four decades in nuclear energy, including leadership roles supporting U.S. Department of Energy initiatives.

team.name: Mike (Michael) Reinboth
team.background: CEO (Treasurer on the 2025 Form Ds). The company site cites executive roles at global enterprises and venture-backed companies in energy and technology, naming no prior employer.

team.name: Nick (Nicholas) Burnett
team.background: COO (September 2026 Form D) or Chief Commercial Officer (team page). Per the site, an attorney with structured finance, mergers and acquisitions and energy project development background.

team.name: Rafael Paz
team.background: Chief Financial Officer, announced 15 April 2026. The company release says he held senior finance leadership roles at NuScale Power and bp.

questions: Who are the single investors behind the $10,000,000 (December 2025) and the $1,000,000 (September 2026), and is the latter a first close on the $25,000,000?
What exactly was acquired from Columbia Basin Consulting Group (IP, test data, people), on what terms, and does FANCO own the EAGL-1 design outright?
Your releases cite HALEU dioxide (April 2026) and mixed oxide and transuranic fuels (May 2026). Which fuel does the first core use, and who supplies it?
Is there a signed customer or site for the Bridge Power phase, and why is the CTO announced in April 2026 not on the team page?
risks: Capital gap. The five Form Ds report $13,687,050 sold, against a plan reported at more than $4 billion. The latest offering had sold $1,000,000 of $25,000,000 at filing.

Early licensing. Nuclear Engineering International called the design conceptual (November 2025) and a 2032 start over-optimistic. Sourced NRC steps are engagement plans and a letter of intent, not license applications.
Commercial traction is unproven. The Denham, AtkinsRéalis and Hyundai E&C announcements mention no equity investment in FANCO, and no source read names a power customer or plant site.
unverified: Neutron Bytes (8 November 2025) cites PitchBook for $2.52 million raised and names Foundt Capital as an investor. No primary source confirms either.
World Nuclear News reports, citing the company's regulatory engagement plan, that the technology portfolio was acquired from Columbia Basin Consulting Group. Terms, dates and amounts are not given.
The company says a PNNL review found the design would be licensable under existing NRC criteria. The PNNL report was not opened, so this is not confirmed.

announcement.what: In a PR Newswire release, the company introduced itself and its Eagle One reactor ahead of an investor summit in Oak Ridge.
